title: the Chinese mythos
audit_comment: THE CHINESE MYTHOS - the D&DG walk round seven, print pp. 37-42: eighteen beings (Shang-Ti, Chao Kung Ming, Chih Sung-Tzu, Chih-Chiang Fyu-Ya, Chung Kuel, Fei Lien and Feng Po the Counts of the Wind, Huan-Ti, Kuan Yin, Lei Kung, Lu Yueh, Ma Yuan, No Cha, Shan Hai Ching, the Spirits of the Air, Tou Mu, Wen Chung, Yen-Wang-Yeh), the celestial bureaucracy doctrine, and the seven devices of the mythos. Zero registry defs touched; the floor holds at 995. The flagged eyeball cells: the Wen Chung hit points (the 2nd-print 213 pinned against the IA 1st-print 273, the Gawaine 112 precedent), the Chih Sung-Tzu size (garbled in both voices, the sentinel pinned), and the Wen Chung 12/21 move (both voices agreeing on an unusual printed slash).
audit_anchor: #include "rules/audits/r854_batch.h"  // R854: R854 Central American mythos audit

banner.title: the Chinese mythos - the D&DG walk round seven, print pp. 37-42: eighteen beings from Shang-Ti the head of the Celestial Bureaucracy to Yen-Wang-Yeh the judge of the dead, the two Counts of the Wind, Ma Yuan the killer of gods, the Spirits of the Air, and the seven devices of the mythos across nine planes.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the extract/ddg tesseract pass (commit cd645b4, pNNN_full.txt + pNNN_tsv.tsv, print = pdf - 1, pages 038-043; the second printing); the collation voice: the archive.org 1st-print derivative (deities-demigods-1st-print, djvu.txt + djvu.xml word geometry at 600dpi). The adjudications: the psionic classes by word geometry (Chao Kung Ming and Chung Kuel the 27px II words, Chih-Chiang Fyu-Ya the 49px VI, Tou Mu the 29px II against the Termux single I, Shang-Ti the single bar I), the size decodes (Shang-Ti 5 foot 4 from the printed 514 cell and Chao Kung Ming 6 foot 2 from the 612 cell - the R853 foot-mark-misread lesson; Kuan Yin 5 feet and D 12, the IA geometry words against the Termux 72 garble), the Wen Chung hit points (the 2nd-print 213 pinned against the IA 1st-print 273 - the Gawaine 112 precedent, flagged), the Spirits appearing 1-100 (the Termux clean read plus the up-to-100 prose against the IA 17-1700 djvu garble), and the Chih Sung-Tzu size (garbled in both voices, the sentinel pinned, flagged for the physical-copy eyeball).

bools.name: dggVastMythologyCaveat
bools.comment: the title caveat: the Chinese mythology is too vast and varied to cover adequately, so the most appropriate deities were chosen

bools.name: dggGreatBureaucracy
bools.comment: the Chinese image of the Heavens is that of a great bureaucracy

bools.name: dggSpecialTaskDeities
bools.comment: many of the deities exist to perform a special task and watch over a special area of life

bools.name: dggSupervisionChains
bools.comment: each god is supervised by a more important deity, responsible for seeing things are done correctly

bools.name: dggEmperorAccountability
bools.comment: every being is accountable to the Emperor of the Heavens

bools.name: dggAnnualReports
bools.comment: every year the gods send reports to their supervisors - promotion or demotion for the year's work is not uncommon

bools.name: dggClericsSupportGovernment
bools.comment: the clerics support the existing mortal government and preach the divinity of their emperor

bools.name: dggEmperorHeadOfChurch
bools.comment: the emperor is head of state and of the church, gifted with high priest powers by the gods

bools.name: dggAtonementBySacrifice
bools.comment: atonement for all sins: sacrificing items of value commensurate with the improper act

bools.name: dggAtonementMayBeDeath
bools.comment: if the deed was severe enough, the atonement might even be death

bools.name: dggTravelPreaching
bools.comment: clerics must travel about the countryside preaching to rich and poor alike

bools.name: dggIronWandRevealsInvisible
bools.comment: the Iron Wand makes all invisible things appear

bools.name: dggIronWandDustDisappearance
bools.comment: it can make one object disappear as dust of disappearance

bools.name: dggIronWandStaffOfStriking
bools.comment: it acts as a staff of striking with unlimited charges

bools.name: dggIronWandGrowsToClimb
bools.comment: it grows to 100" upon command, roughened for easy climbing

bools.name: dggJadeScepterBlocksMaterial
bools.comment: the Jade Scepter of Defending defends the user from any number of material weapons - none may strike its master

bools.name: dggJadeScepterConcentration
bools.comment: while concentrating on defense, no other action may even be contemplated

bools.name: dggWindFireWheelStaffOfMagi
bools.comment: the Wind Fire Wheels shoot fire and/or wind as a staff of the magi, used in large battles the gods fear losing

bools.name: dggWindFireWheelFans
bools.comment: they are 1 foot circular fans, started by a command word from the holder

bools.name: dggCanonCreatesNonmagical
bools.comment: the Canon of Changes allows the reader to create any nonmagical object instantly when the command words are spoken

bools.name: dggCanonImmortalsOnly
bools.comment: only immortals have the constitutional stamina to read the passages for the length of time required

bools.name: dggLightningSwordDancingParity
bools.comment: the Dancing Sword of Lightning behaves as a dancing sword per the DUNGEON MASTERS GUIDE

bools.name: dggLightningSwordUnlimited
bools.comment: it has unlimited charges

bools.name: dggLightningSwordAirDemigods
bools.comment: it is the favorite weapon of the demigods of the air, when they can use it in their turn

bools.name: dggLightningSwordMortalNormal
bools.comment: it performs as a normal sword when held by mortals

bools.name: dggFireGemOncePerTurn
bools.comment: the fire gems fire once per turn when the command words are spoken

bools.name: dggPearlUncontrolled
bools.comment: the Giant Black Pearl negates turbulence of its own accord and cannot be controlled to make it stop

bools.name: dggShangTiSupremeGod
bools.comment: Shang-Ti, supreme god of the heavens, god of the sky and agriculture

bools.name: dggShangTiTravelsAmongMortals
bools.comment: he sometimes travels among mortals as an aged man with a long white beard, dressed in tattered robes

bools.name: dggShangTiFloatsEthereal
bools.comment: he likes to float in the air ethereally, viewing cities and towns and how he is or isn't being worshiped

bools.name: dggShangTiWeaponsReturn
bools.comment: all physical weapon attacks sent through the air at the god will turn and strike the sender

bools.name: dggShangTiShaftRangeSight

bools.name: dggShangTiWeatherControl
bools.comment: as god of the sky and agriculture he has complete control over weather - instantly summoning or banishing any type he desires

bools.name: dggShangTiBureaucracyHead
bools.comment: he is the head of the Celestial Bureaucracy; all the other deities ultimately report to him

bools.name: dggShangTiWordIsLaw
bools.comment: his word is law among all the gods and goddesses regardless of alignment; he is the final arbitrator in any dispute

bools.name: dggChaoWarDemigod
bools.comment: Chao Kung Ming, demigod of war: a very muscular man with bright red skin

bools.name: dggChaoRidesFlyingTiger
bools.comment: he rides a giant flying tiger into battle

bools.name: dggChaoPlaneTravel
bools.comment: this god is able to travel from plane to plane with however many beings he wishes

bools.name: dggChihSungRainLord
bools.comment: Chih Sung-Tzu, lord of rain: a very muscular man who always wears a blue war helm

bools.name: dggChihSungWeatherOnCommand
bools.comment: like Shang-Ti, he can create weather of any type upon command

bools.name: dggChihSungRustsMetal
bools.comment: when any other metal touches his scale mail, that metal completely rusts away (no saving throw)

bools.name: dggChihChiangArcherGod
bools.comment: Chih-Chiang Fyu-Ya, god of archers, punisher of the gods: fiery red scaled skin, a black demonic head with tusks, elephant ears, cloven hooves

bools.name: dggChihChiangHitsAnyTargetInSight

bools.name: dggChihChiangReversesWeapons

bools.name: dggChihChiangShapeChange

bools.name: dggChihChiangAvengeGods

bools.name: dggChungKuelTruthGod
bools.comment: Chung Kuel, god of truth and testing, always dressed in costly robes

bools.name: dggChungKuelWellOfKnowledge
bools.comment: his primary ability: to draw from a well of knowledge so he can meet any test with success, given time to visit his well

bools.name: dggChungKuelSecuresWinning
bools.comment: in any physical contest, if his normal powers will not let him immediately win, he will run and secure the materials that allow him to win, doing nothing else until he does

bools.name: dggChungKuelRodOfCancellation
bools.comment: he also carries a rod of cancellation at all times

bools.name: dggChungKuelRiddleTravels

bools.name: dggChungKuelRiddleRewards
bools.comment: correct answers may earn a reward, perhaps even a limited wish - the more difficult the riddle, the greater the reward

bools.name: dggWindCountsOfTheWind
bools.comment: Fei Lien and Feng Po, the Counts of the Wind, man-shaped beings

bools.name: dggWindCountsRideTheWind

bools.name: dggWindCountsLeatherSacks
bools.comment: they each have a large sack of leather that blows djinn-like whirlwinds when opened

bools.name: dggKuanYinNegateViolence
bools.comment: her main attribute: the ability to negate any single act of violence directed at anyone, once per melee round

bools.name: dggKuanYinNeverHarmfulSpells
bools.comment: she will never use her spells to cause harm

bools.name: dggKuanYinNoViolenceAgainstHer
bools.comment: no act of violence can be directed towards her by any being in the universe - she could walk safely through 500 different types of demons and devils

bools.name: dggKuanYinCommonFolk
bools.comment: her main following is with the common folk, and all may work in her cause and expect to be rewarded someday

bools.name: dggKuanYinPeacemakers
bools.comment: her clerics are the peacemakers of the world and work diligently for the end of violence

bools.name: dggLeiKungThunderDuke
bools.comment: Lei Kung, duke of thunder: a man with smoking black skin and eyes with pupils like lightning bolts, 2 large tusks and a huge nose

bools.name: dggLeiKungGreenDrums
bools.comment: when battling large numbers of opponents he uses a set of green drums that act as a horn of blasting and drums of panic combined

bools.name: dggLeiKungFoulWeatherOnRequest
bools.comment: he exists to make foul weather of one type or another at the request of the other gods, when their worshipers need a lesson

bools.name: dggLeiKungDelightsInWindstorms
bools.comment: he particularly delights in creating wind storms that destroy fragile things of beauty or value

bools.name: dggLuYuehEpidemicGod
bools.comment: Lu Yueh, god of epidemics: 3 demon-like heads, 6 arms ending in claws, green scaled skin, a look of death and an odor of putrescence

bools.name: dggLuYuehRottingSicknessSpell
bools.comment: his main attribute: a rotting sickness spell that kills his enemies who fail a saving throw versus poison in 2 melee rounds

bools.name: dggLuYuehNoArmor
bools.comment: he never wears armor because all wounds instantly close themselves

bools.name: dggMaYuanGodKiller
bools.comment: Ma Yuan, killer of the gods: a unique monster with 3 eyes in his tyrannosaurus-shaped head and 4 large humanoid arms

bools.name: dggMaYuanStormGiantStrength
bools.comment: he has the strength of a storm giant but rarely relies on this in battle

bools.name: dggMaYuanTriangularStone
bools.comment: he has a powerful magical device shaped as a small triangular piece of stone that turns into any weapon the holder wishes, magical or otherwise

bools.name: dggMaYuanDoublePowerTactic
bools.comment: his favorite tactic: to make a weapon from his stone that is double the power of the one being used against him

bools.name: dggMaYuanPreventsComplacency
bools.comment: the existence of Ma Yuan prevents complacency among the gods

bools.name: dggNoChaThievesDemigod
bools.comment: No Cha, demigod of thieves: a three-headed, eight-armed man with silvery scaled skin and eyes that blaze like fire

bools.name: dggNoChaGrowShrink
bools.comment: he has the ability to grow or shrink in size

bools.name: dggNoChaPantherWhirlwind
bools.comment: his panther skin bag blows a whirlwind like that of a djinni

bools.name: dggNoChaStranglerBracelet
bools.comment: his thrown bracelet attaches itself to the neck of its target and strangles him or her

bools.name: dggNoChaThievesPatron
bools.comment: No Cha is the patron of thieves, and there are many tales of his famous thieving exploits

bools.name: dggShanHaiWindSeaGod
bools.comment: Shan Hai Ching, god of wind and sea: a roc's body with the oversized head of a man

bools.name: dggShanHaiHurricaneWind
bools.comment: the power to raise up a hurricane wind - said to last a full day when great wrath is upon the deity

bools.name: dggShanHaiSeaSummoning
bools.comment: the power to call forth any creature of the sea (of non-divine nature) to do his bidding; the summoning will seem to create beings from the very water

bools.name: dggShanHaiSpellTurning
bools.comment: one spell attack against him per round will be turned back upon the caster; if multiple spells are cast, the one turned is chosen at random

bools.name: dggShanHaiSeaSacrifice
bools.comment: he and his clerics serve all beings using the sea, and any trip out into the oceans requires a sacrifice to this deity for good winds and the like

bools.name: dggSpiritsOfTheAir
bools.comment: the Spirits of the Air: very rare minions of the wind gods

bools.name: dggSpiritsLook
bools.comment: they have black skin, large bat wings, clawed feet (which they use in battle), and a tusked monkey's head

bools.name: dggTouMuNorthStarGoddess
bools.comment: Tou Mu, goddess of the north star

bools.name: dggTouMuDancingSword
bools.comment: she wields a +3 dancing sword

bools.name: dggTouMuMoonPiece
bools.comment: a piece of the moon is able to block any single hit directed at her person in any given melee round

bools.name: dggTouMuLotusHeals
bools.comment: a lotus flower heals all wounds at a touch

bools.name: dggTouMuFreeClaws
bools.comment: her free claws do 1-10 points of damage per hit

bools.name: dggTouMuAdamantChariots
bools.comment: the chariots are all of adamant with gold figures of dragons; the wheels are of unbreakable green jade and sparks fly from them whenever they run over beings in battle

bools.name: dggWenChungThunderMinister
bools.comment: Wen Chung, minister of thunder: 3 eyes in his head and a massive dark-skinned body

bools.name: dggWenChungSummonsWeather
bools.comment: he summons weather for Lei Kung and for his chaotic worshipers

bools.name: dggWenChungImmunities
bools.comment: he is totally immune to lightning, cold, or light attacks

bools.name: dggYenWangDeadJudge
bools.comment: Yen-Wang-Yeh, judge of the dead: a warrior with black skin

bools.name: dggYenWangDragonShape
bools.comment: in battle he likes to shape change into an oriental dragon and use its powers for dealing out death

bools.name: dggYenWangTouchParalysis
bools.comment: anyone touching his body with anything will become paralyzed (saving throw applicable)

bools.name: dggYenWangCollectsSouls
bools.comment: he collects all the souls and spirits of the dead, transports them to the proper plane, and makes sure they do not roam the earth at will

bools.name: dggYenWangTracksRogues
bools.comment: he tracks down spirits that do roam and makes them suffer for eternity

bools.name: dggYenWangNoPowerOverRisen
bools.comment: he has no power over the dead who have risen to a higher plane through their good deeds

tables.name: the combat grid
col_comments: The armor class cells (Huan-Ti the printed -7, Chih-Chiang the printed +7)
The range ceiling cells (0 = a single printed armor class; all eighteen read single this round)
The hit point cells (400 for Shang-Ti down to 50 per Spirit)
The primary move cells (the printed moves; Huan-Ti 18, Shan Hai Ching 6)
The secondary move cells (the printed slash ceilings; Wen Chung the printed 12/21, both voices agreeing)
The attack count cells (Huan-Ti the printed 2 or 4; Tou Mu and No Cha 8, Lu Yueh 6, Ma Yuan 5)
The attack alternative cells (the 3/2 slashes and Huan-Ti's or-4 ceiling)
The magic resistance cells (0 = the printed Standard of Chih Sung-Tzu, the Counts and Lu Yueh; Kuan Yin the printed 100%)

The size cells in inches (Shang-Ti 5'4" the 514 decode and Chao 6'2" the 612 decode - the R853 foot-mark lesson; Chih Sung-Tzu the sentinel, garbled in both voices - flagged; the monsters Ma Yuan 70', Spirits 8')
tables.audit_comment: the combat stat blocks of the eighteen beings (print pp. 37-42) - the armor classes, hit points, moves, attacks, magic resistance and sizes

tables.name: the class grid
col_comments: The cleric level cells (0 = Nil; Kuan Yin the 25th level cleric)
The druid level cells (Lei Kung and No Cha the 10th level druids; the 14s)
The fighter level floor cells (0 = the ranger-slot beings, Kuan Yin's Nil, and the monster rows)
The fighter level ceiling cells (single printed levels read floor = ceiling)
The ranger level cells (Chao 17, Chung Kuel 20, Huan-Ti 20, the Counts 10, Tou Mu 15, Wen Chung 10)
The magic-user level cells (99 = the printed See below: Kuan Yin the 20th level magic-user doctrine)
The illusionist level cells (No Cha the 17th level illusionist over a Nil magic-user)
The thief level cells (the Counts 10th, Lu Yueh the 19th level thief, No Cha the 20th)
The assassin level cells (the 15s; Chao 10th, Wen Chung-era none)
The monk level cells (Chao 7, the Counts 5, Huan-Ti 12, Chih-Chiang 10, Chung Kuel 10, Yen-Wang-Yeh 12)
The bard level cells (Shang-Ti 15th, Kuan Yin 15th, Chih-Chiang and Chung Kuel 10)
tables.audit_comment: the five-slot class grid of the eighteen beings (the printed See below, the ranger slots, the demigod monk abilities)

tables.name: the ability grid
col_comments: The strength cells (Kuan Yin the printed S:8, Yen-Wang-Yeh and the Counts 14)
The parenthesized strength to-hit bonus cells (0 = no printed bracket)
The parenthesized strength damage bonus cells (the +14s of the S:25s)
The intelligence cells (Tou Mu W:3 and No Cha W:7 the low wisdoms ride the int col commentary; the printed I line)
The wisdom cells (No Cha the printed W:7, Tou Mu the printed W:3)
The dexterity cells (Kuan Yin the printed D:12 - the IA geometry word against the Termux 72 garble)
The constitution cells (the 25s)
The charisma cells (Chih-Chiang the printed -2 and Lu Yueh the printed -3; Lei Kung 7, the Counts 9)
The psionic score cells (0 = no numeric scores; the monster rows read the all-sentinel line)
tables.audit_comment: the six ability scores with the strength brackets of the eighteen beings (the monster rows read the all-sentinel line)

tables.name: the roster grid
col_comments: The roster ordinal cells (the print order, Shang-Ti through Yen-Wang-Yeh)
The print page cells (37-42, the folio offset PRINT = PDF - 1)
The alignment cells (0 LG, 1 NG, 2 CG, 3 LN, 4 N, 5 CN Wen Chung, 6 LE, 7 NE No Cha, 8 CE - the R852 code scheme)
The rank cells (0 lesser, 1 greater, 2 demigod, 3 monster format - Ma Yuan and the Spirits)
The psionic class cells (0 Nil the monsters, 1 Shang-Ti, 2 Chao/Chung Kuel/Tou Mu, 5 the Counts, 6 the ten VI readers - the R849 class table)
The plane cells (1 Nirvana, 2 Elemental Plane of Air, 3 Gehenna, 4 Seven Heavens, 5 Limbo, 6 Acheron, 7 Abyss, 8 Nine Hells, 9 Concordant Opposition; 0 = the monster rows)
The fixed-damage flags (1 = the printed DAMAGE/ATTACK cell is numeric damage; 0 = Nil, See below, or Variable)
The in-each flags (the printed Nth level in each cells: the M-U/I pairs and the monk/bard in-eachs)
The twin-pair flags (Fei Lien and Feng Po, the identical Counts of the Wind stat blocks)
tables.audit_comment: the roster walk of the eighteen beings - ordinals, pages, alignments, ranks, psionic classes, the nine planes, the fixed-damage, in-each and twin-pair flags
